newsitem.title: UK: Half UK barley harvested, wheat started.
newsitem.headline: Half UK barley harvested, wheat started.

text.p: After a weekend of good weather in southern areas British farmers have got around half the barley crop in, analysts said.
And some wheat has been harvested in southern areas.

Although it was beginning to look as though the overall barley yield might be down on 1996's performance, an increased area is likely to mean that last year's crop will be matched or even beaten, an expert at the agricultural advisory service ADAS said.

According to ministry figures, the 1996 UK barley crop was 7.78 million tonnes. And according to Home Grown Cereals Authority estimates the area planted for the 1997 crop for the UK as a whole was up by 5.7 percent at 1.338 million hectares.
"I don't think the yield's gone down by as much as the area's gone up," the ADAS expert said.
First cuts of wheat gave widely varying impressions of quality and yields, just as the barley had done, he said.
